subject: Partner catalog onboarding + account routing plan for Catalyst integration
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@catalystisv.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: integrations@catalystisv.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Introduction: Catalyst x Redwood — integration + GTM mapping

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this — I lead integrations at Catalyst (ISV partner building a connector marketplace for enterprise apps). We’ve worked with a few LLM providers; Redwood’s runtime performance and deployment options look like a strong fit for our connector that needs consistent latency in multi-tenant SaaS environments.

Two asks to get started:
- Can we map which of our anchor accounts overlap with Redwood direct sales or existing partners? We have ~25 target accounts for H1; I attached a compact integration matrix for reference.
- Can you share a recommended onboarding + routing approach so we avoid territory conflict — ideally a clear rule set for account ownership vs. partner-led deals?

High level timeline we’re aiming for: catalog listing + tech validation in Dec, pilot in Jan, expanded GTM in Q1. Would love to set a 30m sync this week.

Attachments: catalyst-integration-matrix.xlsx

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Integrations | Catalyst Technologies
email: lena.ortiz@catalystisv.com
mobile: +1 (415) 555-0199

-----

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Introduction: Catalyst x Redwood — integration + GTM mapping

Folks — forwarding a partner inbound. Catalyst wants to onboard to our catalog and needs a routing/ownership playbook to avoid stepping on sales. Key asks: account overlap mapping and a lightweight onboarding plan.

My suggested approach (initial):
1) Quick overlap scan: Marissa, can your AM reports run the 25 names vs. existing active deals/ARR > $50k? Highlight any deals in negotiation or Renewal windows.
2) Routing rule proposal:
   - If Redwood has an active opportunity (deal stage > Demo/Proposal) we retain ownership and offer partner technical enablement + margin split.
   - If no active Redwood opportunity, partner-led with Redwood as technology provider; partner gets lead credit and listing promotion.
   - If an account is co-owned historically, default to the team with the most recent engagement (last 90 days) unless there's an exec escalation.
3) Catalog onboarding: Sergio, technical checklist: test account creation flow, token provisioning, sample connector validating latency to 95th pct under 500ms for target sequences.

I’ll draft a short mutual action plan for Catalyst and propose a 30m sync (Wed or Thu). Marissa — can you surface the overlap report by EOD? Sergio — can you confirm the technical checklist items and whether the pilot infra is available in early Jan?

Thanks,
Hannah
Director, Alliances | Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 13:20:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Introduction: Catalyst x Redwood — integration + GTM mapping

Hi Lena — really excited to work with Catalyst. Appreciate the matrix (reviewed it briefly). Below is a concise onboarding + routing plan we can use as the basis for a short mutual action plan (MAP). If this looks good I’ll paste into a shared doc and we can track owners/dates.

Proposed MAP summary (high level):
1) Account overlap & ownership
   - Marissa will run overlap against open Redwood opportunities (> $50k ARR) and flag any conflicts by EOD today.
   - For flagged accounts: 3-way review with partner + Deal Owner + Alliances to decide co-sell vs. Redwood retain.
2) Catalog & technical validation (Dec)
   - Sergio to provide a technical checklist (below) and a sandbox token for Catalyst by 12/07.
   - Catalyst to deliver connector smoke test results and latency report by 12/18.
3) Pilot & GTM (Jan)
   - Pilot: 4-week pilot in a non-prod slice of 2 anchor customers (mutually agreed).
   - GTM: joint listing in our partner catalog, co-marketing asset, and lead routing setup (HubSpot mapping).
4) Commercial routing rules (routing examples):
   - Partner-initiated inbound: if partner produces the initial opportunity (first-touch in HubSpot), partner gets lead credit and nurture ownership for 30 days; Redwood can request co-sell if ARR profile meets threshold.
   - Redwood-initiated outbound: Redwood field owns the opportunity but will involve partner as delivery vendor with referral margin.

Technical checklist (Sergio) — items to confirm:
- Sandbox API key + token scopes for connector validation
- Example prompt/seqs for 95th pct latency test (100-token avg sample)
- KV cache behavior and recommended per-tenant settings
- Error handling & fallback behavior (model variants on capacity constraints)
- Minimal SLO targets and telemetry hooks for Catalyst to send to their monitoring

Attachments provided: Catalyst matrix reviewed. I’m attaching a draft SOW template for Catalyst to review (Catalyst_Redwood_SOW_v1.pdf) — light commercial terms; procurement/legal can iterate.

Next steps:
- Marissa: overlap report by EOD.
- Sergio: confirm checklist + sandbox token ETA (aim 12/07).
- Lena: confirm preferred sync time (Wed 12/02 10am PT or Thu 12/03 2pm PT) and which two anchor accounts you prefer for the pilot.

Thanks — I’ll open a shared MAP doc and HubSpot deal (link below) once we have the overlap report.

Best,
Hannah
Director, Alliances | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Catalyst_Redwood_SOW_v1.pdf

Links: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/HS-45678
